helped: Kazakh pretrained encoders: KazBERT 0.860 form, kaz-roberta 0.629 area (+0.03 to +0.05 over TF-IDF, CI excludes 0)
MLM pretraining + distillation for the 5.2M tiny model: form 0.793 → 0.827, area 0.584 → 0.598
Kazakh vocabulary pruning: e5 118M → 25.5M (−78 %) at equal F1 (0.845 vs 0.842)
kaz-roberta with layer-wise LR decay + recency weighting: area 0.622 → 0.629; train+val refit 0.634
Word + char n-grams for TF-IDF: 0.820 vs 0.803 (word) / 0.778 (char)
not_helped: Kazakh suffix stemming: 0.783 vs 0.803 for word forms (suffixes carry signal)
Deeper tiny model: 4 vs 2 layers within seed noise (±0.012–0.019 std)
Seq2seq label generation (mT5, 58.7M): 0.791 form, below TF-IDF
LLM teacher Qwen3-1.7B: 0.775 form, weaker than every encoder; Sherkala-8B is gated
Stronger teacher for the tiny student (kaz-roberta vs e5): +0.002, within noise
Ensembles and prior-shift correction: all families fail on the same hard titles
error_points: Шешім → Қаулы (423) and Бұйрық → Қаулы (334) dominate: same topics, the title rarely names the issuer type
Titles far from any train title (cosine < 0.6): 17 % errors vs 0.8 % for near-duplicates
Very short titles (1–10 words): 9.1 % errors vs 1.3 % for 21–30 words
Confidence ≥ 0.9 covers 97 % of titles at 97.7 % accuracy → route the rest to manual review
conclusions: A 5.2M tiny transformer from scratch needs MLM + distillation to tie TF-IDF on form; then it beats it on area and matches the 118M e5-small at about 1/7 of the CPU latency
Kazakh encoders (KazBERT, kaz-roberta) are best within 120M: +0.03 to +0.05 macro-F1
Vocabulary pruning cuts e5 by 78 % for free; seq2seq and the LLM teacher did not pay off
54 % of test titles are templated near-duplicates and the error rate grows yearly, so temporal + strict evaluation and CIs are essential
efficiency_note: CPU latency: unified benchmark (batch 64, 8 threads, median of 3) on a shared machine; absolute values vary by about ±20 %. F1 = macro-F1 on test_strict.
